citation.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network-based Topology Optimization (PINNTO) framework for structural optimization
citation.authors: Hyogu Jeong; Jinshuai Bai; C. P. Batuwatta-Gamage; Charith Rathnayaka; Ying Zhou; YuanTong Gu
citation.version_coded: QUT repository author manuscript (accepted manuscript); version of record metadata confirmed

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: In the first full-text quantitative comparison, PINNTO uses substantially more wall-clock time than SIMP despite broadly similar objective values across four cases.
claim.key_phrase: computational time requirements for PINNTO exceeds that of the SIMP method
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Case 1 total time: SIMP 0.81 s / PINNTO 915.02 s = 0.000885x (Table 1); this is a slowdown, not a speed-up.
claim.alternatives: For 3D Case 6, the text reports similar topology and less than 5% objective-value difference with significantly fewer PINNTO iterations, but Table 1 reports much longer PINNTO wall time in its four 2D cases.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP topology optimization (Liu and Tovar 3D SIMP code for the 3D case)
baseline.implementation: SIMP code; implementation details not stated for the four 2D cases; Liu and Tovar code for 3D case
baseline.solver: SIMP with finite-element analysis; PINNTO replaces the FEA state solution with an energy-based PINN
baseline.problem_size: Four 2D cases in Table 1; 3D case uses 60x20x4 hexahedral mesh (Sec. 4.6)
baseline.classical_iterations: Table 1: 35, 49, 67, 11 iterations for SIMP across Cases 1-4
baseline.classical_time: 0.81 s, 1.19 s, 1.56 s, 0.31 s total for Cases 1-4, respectively (Table 1)
baseline.ml_time: 915.02 s, 1,581.02 s, 2,176.68 s, 398.86 s total for Cases 1-4, respectively (Table 1)
baseline.training_time: Per-problem PINN fitting; loss convergence begins after about 20 epochs in Fig. 9; elapsed training time not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: not applicable; per-problem learning without offline training
baseline.quality_metric: mean compliance/objective value and topology comparison (Sec. 4, Table 1; Sec. 4.6, Fig. 18)
baseline.quality_gap: First three Table 1 cases: objective-value difference under 3%; Case 4: 5.51%; 3D case reports less than 5% difference (Secs. 4 and 4.6).

R1.evidence: Sec. 4/Table 1 reports both wall times and objective values for four cases, but does not establish a matched-time budget or a quality tolerance for the comparisons; the 3D comparison is separately described as under 5% objective difference (Sec. 4.6).

R2.evidence: Table 1 shows SIMP wall time is much lower than PINNTO, but no article text establishes an inefficient SIMP setup, per-iteration time against our strong baseline, or a qualifying hardware mismatch.

R3.evidence: Sec. 3 embeds PINN learning in each topology-optimization problem; there is no offline training dataset or separate model-training phase.

R4.evidence: Secs. 2-3 evaluate structural state through the energy-based PINN in place of FEA; no failure or infeasibility rate for returned PINNTO designs is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Four 2D cases compared in Table 1, plus further 2D and 3D examples in Sec. 4

notes: The version of record PDF returned 403, but the QUT institutional repository supplied the author's accepted manuscript. Table 1 shows PINNTO is slower than SIMP in all four listed 2D cases.
